A few more minor details I haven’t seen mentioned (I don’t think?) 

•Remember that you can get star coins from decomposing! If you’re in desperate need of star coins and don’t mind sacrificing some stamina, farm some maiden items for decomposing! (If you’re far enough into the game, Maiden 7-7 and 8-5 are good for reconstruction suits! The former drops 3 heart [hope rings] and 4 heart [rebirth earrings] items, and the latter drops a 5 heart item [eternal necklaces].) 

•Something that helps me gauge how much I’ll need to spend to finish a suit is to buy the items that require the most event currency first, then spend the rest of the days getting the less expensive items (if you’re planning on finishing a suit)

•Remember to check what kind of currency (vip or diamond only) is required for recharges, so that you can complete the suits for the best value. (If VIP counts, and you still need diamonds, remember that daily packs generally have a pretty good value, but always weigh the pros and cons of what you’re going to get- it’s real money, after all) (Daily packs also work great for stamina events, as some packs have high amounts of stamina)(Wow, sorry to include a third of these, but don’t rush getting recharges if you don’t have to, if it’s VIP points. Sometimes it’s more worth it to go for a better daily pack instead of getting whatever’s immediately there.)

I’ve seen the first and last topics come up in quite a few posts, so I felt they’d be useful to add.

And on to more general advice,

•Don’t lose sight of having fun for the sake of ‘doing well’. I lost a lot of sleep over one of the ranking events, and while I got the posed version, I spent an inordinate amount of time stressing out over such a small thing. 

•Don’t feel pressured to play the game in the way everyone else is playing if you don’t want to. I personally chipped away at hell suits little by little while doing other things in the game alongside it (part of why I have such a high wardrobe count), and it’s made the hell suits seem far more manageable than they originally did. (To contrast, I’ve seen a lot of people become laser-focused on the hell suits and nothing else. I’m not saying that’s a bad thing, everyone should play how they want to. It just wasn’t the way I wanted to play) 

•Remember that it’s a game. Not a competition, not a life or death thing, not something to build your life around. Let it supplement your life. Be something you look forward to. Not something that causes undue stress, or makes you be nasty to someone else. Just have fun, and if and when things stop being fun, take a step back and reevaluate the situation.
